title: Accuracy harness with gold answers
description: The tool runs over a labeled task set with known-correct gold answers, and each output is scored as exact match, partial match, or miss. Accuracy is reported with the task count so readers can judge significance. Gold sets are versioned so scores stay comparable across tool versions. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers scoring outputs against gold answers.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: 10, 2: 25, 3: 50}
N = CFG[LEVEL]
import random
random.seed(11)
gold = [i % 4 for i in range(N)]
pred = [g if random.random() < 0.8 else (g + 1) % 4 for g in gold]
acc = sum(1 for g, p in zip(gold, pred) if g == p) / N
print("tasks:", N, "| accuracy: %.2f" % acc)
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Latency percentile profiling
description: The tool is run many times and the latency distribution is summarized with percentiles: p50 for the typical case, p95 and p99 for the tail. Percentiles reveal slow outliers that averages hide. Warmup runs are discarded so JIT and cache effects do not pollute the numbers. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers measuring p50/p95/p99 over repeated runs.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: 100, 2: 500, 3: 1000}
N = CFG[LEVEL]
import random, time
random.seed(3)
lat = sorted(random.gammavariate(2, 0.01) for _ in range(N))
def pct(p): return lat[int(p * N)]
print("n=%d p50=%.3fs p95=%.3fs p99=%.3fs" % (N, pct(0.50), pct(0.95), pct(0.99)))
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Resource consumption metering
description: Peak memory and CPU time are measured per task using OS counters, so benchmarks report what a tool costs, not just how fast it is. Memory is sampled at peak RSS; CPU time separates user and system. Resource numbers make capacity planning possible. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers measuring peak memory per task.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: 1000, 2: 10000, 3: 100000}
N = CFG[LEVEL]
import tracemalloc, time
tracemalloc.start()
t0 = time.perf_counter()
data = [i * i for i in range(N)]
total = sum(data)
cpu = time.perf_counter() - t0
peak_kb = tracemalloc.get_traced_memory()[1] / 1024
tracemalloc.stop()
print("n=%d sum=%d cpu=%.4fs peak=%.1fKB" % (N, total, cpu, peak_kb))
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Reliability (success-rate) tracking
description: The tool runs N trials and the success rate is reported with a binomial confidence interval, so a 95 percent success rate over 20 trials is not confused with the same rate over 20,000 trials. Reliability tracking separates flaky tools from solid ones with statistical honesty. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers success rates with confidence intervals.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: (18, 20), 2: (190, 200), 3: (1900, 2000)}
ok, n = CFG[LEVEL]
import math
p = ok / n
margin = 1.96 * math.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n)
print("success %d/%d = %.3f | 95%% CI [%.3f, %.3f]" % (ok, n, p, p - margin, p + margin))
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Head-to-head A/B benchmark
description: Two tools run the same workload and their outputs are compared pair by pair: wins, losses, and ties. Paired comparison controls for task difficulty, so the winner is the better tool, not the luckier draw. Significance is checked before declaring a winner. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers paired comparison on identical workloads.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: 20, 2: 60, 3: 200}
N = CFG[LEVEL]
import random
random.seed(5)
wins = sum(1 for _ in range(N) if random.random() < 0.62)
print("tool A wins %d/%d (%.1f%%)" % (wins, N, 100.0 * wins / N), "| winner:", "A" if wins > N / 2 else "tie")
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.
